title: A Message to a Friend
description: Practise can, be and have got, and write a short message to a friend.
instructions: Do the exercises in Part 1. Then write your text in Part 2.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word.
exercises.text: ___ you come to my house after school?
exercises.explanation: Use "Can you + base verb?" to ask if someone is able to do something: Can you come?

exercises.prompt: Write the negative form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: I ___ (not / be) at home this afternoon.
exercises.explanation: The negative of "I am" is "I am not" (I'm not).

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: We can meet at four o'clock.
At four o'clock we can meet.
Can we meet at four o'clock?
exercises.explanation: Subject + can + base verb + time: We can meet at four o'clock.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: Have you got my book? I needs it for school.
answers: Have you got my book? I need it for school.
exercises.explanation: With I, the verb has no -s: I need.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best word to join the ideas.
exercises.text: I can't come to football ___ I am ill.
exercises.explanation: "Because" gives the reason: I can't come because I am ill.

exercises.prompt: Write one word to complete the question.
exercises.text: ___ you got a pen for me?
exercises.explanation: Make questions with have got like this: Have you got ...?

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word.
exercises.explanation: Use "on" with days of the week: on Friday.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: I have got two new comic for you.
answers: I have got two new comics for you.
exercises.explanation: After a number bigger than one, add -s to the noun: two comics.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
exercises.explanation: This + is + noun: This is my phone number.

exercises.prompt: Complete with my, his, her, our or their.
exercises.text: Tom and Sara are at ___ grandmother's house today.
exercises.explanation: Use "their" for something that belongs to two or more people (they): their grandmother.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word.
exercises.text: My sister ___ got a new phone.
exercises.explanation: Use "has got" with he, she and it: my sister has got.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: We is at the park now.
answers: We are at the park now.
exercises.explanation: Use "are" with we, you and they: we are.

exercises.prompt: Write a or an.
exercises.text: Can you bring ___ apple for me?
exercises.explanation: Use "an" before a vowel sound: an apple.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
exercises.explanation: Use "at" for a meeting place: meet me at the park.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word.
exercises.text: I can come on Saturday, ___ I can't come on Sunday.
exercises.explanation: Use "but" to join two different or opposite ideas.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: Do your brother want to come?
answers: Does your brother want to come?
exercises.explanation: Use "does" in questions with he, she and it: Does your brother want ...?

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word.
exercises.text: This is ___ book. Can you give it to her?
exercises.explanation: Add 's to a name to show that something belongs to that person: Anna's book.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: Can you to help me with my homework?
answers: Can you help me with my homework?
exercises.explanation: After "can", use the verb without "to": Can you help me?

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
exercises.explanation: Like + verb-ing, and add -s for he/she: my brother likes swimming.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the negative form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.explanation: Make the present simple negative with I + don't (do not) + verb: I don't have.

task.prompt: You can't meet your friend today. Write a message to your friend.
contentPoints: Say sorry that you can't meet today.
Suggest another day and time to meet.
task.modelAnswer:
Hi Leo,

I'm sorry, but I can't come to the park today because I have a cold. Can we meet on Saturday at ten o'clock? We can play football and then go to my house. Is that OK?

Tom
